Source: A 26-year-old woman presents to the emergency department because she feels as though her heart is "beating out of her chest."
After unsuccessful attempts at vagal maneuvers, the emergency physician administers an IV medication.
Her temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 124/84 mmHg, pulse is 180/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
She states that she feels well apart from the discomfort of that sensation.
The effect of the medication wears off in seconds.
